analysis.title: Fixed Income Weekly Update (November 16th, 2026)
key_insights: Treasuries had their sharpest weekly selloff in over a year, ending five straight weekly gains. The 2yr yield rose 33 bp to 4.84% and the 10yr rose 28 bp to 5.14%, the highest 10yr close in over four weeks.
The curve bear flattened. 2s/10s ended at 0.29%, 5.1 bp tighter on the week, and the 30yr rose 20.1 bp to 5.47%, so short maturities led the move.
October CPI was hotter than forecast. Headline rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, each 0.1 point above forecast, and this reinforced expectations of prolonged Fed tightening.

Fed officials signaled more hikes. Waller raised the possibility of a 50 bp December hike, Logan called for two more 25 bp increases, and Schmid, Hammack and Collins also backed further tightening. Markets are pricing rising odds of a 50 bp December hike.
Treasury refunding auctions drew disappointing demand, which the report says raises concerns about investor appetite for duration.

The U.S. started fiscal 2027 with a record $404 billion October deficit, up 42% year over year and about $105 billion above the $299 billion consensus. Outlays rose 12% to $773 billion and receipts fell 9% to $369 billion. Interest cost was about $103 billion, or 28 cents of each tax dollar collected in October. Piper says the gap will likely add to borrowing needs and could keep long-term yields elevated.
Risk appetite improved while bonds sold off. The S&P 500 rose 2.5% on the week to 7561.7 and high-yield spreads tightened 30 bp. Gold fell 4.6% to $3,884.5 and oil fell 2.5% to $88.6.

Factors cited for a Treasury rally: falling crude and the IEA's growing oil-surplus outlook, Nvidia leadership turmoil and weakness in AI-related equities that could draw flight-to-quality buying, and a softer PPI that lowered October core PCE estimates from 0.35% to 0.3%.
October existing-home sales fell 5.5% to 3.75 million annualized units, the lowest since 2010. Friday's headline PPI (final demand +0.3% against a prior 1.3%) came in softer than expected.

The week of Nov 16 to 20 is busy. Nvidia reports earnings after the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang, and October retail sales, industrial production and housing data are due. FOMC minutes on Wednesday and several Fed speakers will be watched for the pace of further tightening.

The Loan Strategies section lists primary-market loan yields, such as 30yr prime jumbo residential at 6.875% and BSL corporate BBB at 6.05%. It also lists active and closed pool transactions. This is product marketing with no market view.
earnings_insights: Nvidia is scheduled to report earnings during the week of Nov 16, described as taking center stage after the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang. The report gives no EPS or revenue estimates.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling crude and the IEA's growing oil-surplus outlook could reduce inflation risk premiums. Nvidia turmoil and AI equity weakness could bring flight-to-quality buying. Softer PPI lowered core PCE estimates, and existing-home sales fell to the lowest since 2010.
tension_points.bear_case: Hotter October CPI, hawkish Fed speakers and expectations of a 50 bp December hike support higher yields. A record $404 bn deficit and weak refunding auction demand raise concerns about appetite for duration.
